title: org.ligatureprotocol.capability.clipboard
description: DRAFT. The clipboard capability (spec chapter 05 section 3b): user-scoped. A clipboard holds one selection in several representations at once; a set carries the plain text and a list of parts, each a MIME type with either the bytes (pushed, within the receiver's maxBytes) or a file descriptor of the files capability (announced, fetched over a files transfer only when an application pastes). A selection of files is always announced. A get asks the peer for its current value, answered with a set. The receiver applies the newest set by setAt and never re-sends what it just applied.

params.description: The descriptor's params for this capability.

maxBytes.description: The push bound: the largest total of text and pushed part bytes this device accepts in one set. Never more than the frame limit of ADR 0036 less 64 KiB of headroom; a part above what fits is announced instead.

mimeTypes.description: The content types this device accepts and can put on its clipboard. A sender includes only parts whose mime the receiver lists; text/plain travels as text regardless.

fetch.description: Whether this device holds a promise for an announced part and fetches it over a files transfer when an application pastes. A device without it is sent only what fits in maxBytes and no file parts.

part.description: One representation of the selection: the bytes themselves, or a descriptor of the files capability to fetch them by, with its sha256 required.

bytes.description: The representation, pushed. Base64url unpadded in JSON, a byte string in CBOR.

file.description: The representation, announced: the sender offers it under this id for the availability window, and the receiver fetches it on paste and checks the hash.

set.description: The sender's clipboard now holds this value. With neither text, parts nor files it says the clipboard emptied.

text.description: The plain-text representation, present whenever the source offers plain text.

parts.description: The other representations, pushed or announced; at most one per mime.

files.description: A selection of files, always announced: fetched over a files transfer on paste.

setAt.description: When the sender's clipboard took this value; the newest wins.

get.description: Asks the peer for its current clipboard value; the peer answers with a set, empty when it holds nothing it may send.
